cold_sampling.save_arrival_model: one writer coroutine; next save starts only after previous commit returns; not fixed-rate open-loop load

warm_sampling.ordering: after all cold concurrent saves, paused-reader save, and awaited LibraryTextIndex.build
warm_sampling.background_competition: probe uses read(), not observe(); its warm section launches no index builder or writer

path_differences.baseline: Room transaction for search; request preloads all 10,010,000 note-body characters and warm matching uses those Kotlin strings
path_differences.candidate: separate deferred read-only WAL snapshot; authoritative candidate note bodies are loaded on demand for each query, then matched by Kotlin Unicode contains through SQLite callback
path_differences.notes_fts: none on either revision; existing FTS covers page and card sources

interpretation: The same offered serial-save workload has different overlap: the baseline writer first waits for the search transaction, then can issue remaining saves after search; the candidate permits saves during scanning.
The higher candidate save p50/p95 therefore includes different actual overlap and shared CPU competition; this probe alone does not isolate intrinsic save-path cost.
Warm regression is measured after writes/indexing finish and cannot be explained by those probe tasks running concurrently.
Extra snapshot and candidate-body read/JNI costs are consistent with warm regression; without stage timing their individual contributions are unmeasured.
One or two matched runs are exploratory measurements on a software emulator, not a statistical confidence claim or physical-device performance result.
Concurrent CPU/I/O work and a pinned WAL snapshot can contribute to changed overlap costs; no stage trace isolates their contributions.
local_opportunity_review: Cheap tag/page/card matches could short-circuit before body reading, but this fixture has one page hit; skipping one body read is insufficient to explain or eliminate the measured difference. No cache/index framework or freshness compromise added.
repeat_plan: Run the identical already-built probe again on candidate then baseline, using the same software emulator, final signed APKs and fresh synthetic databases. Preserve both runs separately; do not pool medians.
ui_scope: Repository-level probe: initial headers are read with Flow.first(); no live shelf/header UI collector is kept during the 30 saves. This does not measure full application UI rendering or repeated header invalidation work.
